newsitem.title: USA: TALKING POINT/PepsiCo profits boost stock.
newsitem.headline: TALKING POINT/PepsiCo profits boost stock.

text.p: PepsiCo Inc shares rose over nine percent on Tuesday after stronger-than-expected quarterly results boosted Wall Street's confidence in the company and its restructuring plan.
"I think this indicates the turn from PepsiCo that investors have been waiting for," PaineWebber analyst Emanuel Goldman said.
PepsiCo shares were up 2-7/8 to 34-1/8 on volume of 5.6 million shares by late morning. Average daily volume for PepsiCo is 3.3 million shares.
"That's a huge move for Pepsi," Goldman said. "This may be the highest volume stock today when all is said and done."
PepsiCo reported net income of $0.27 per share, $0.03 higher than for the same period a year ago and also $0.03 above the analysts' consensus estimate.
"The numbers are excellent," said Martin Romm, a Credit Suisse First Boston analyst. "I think you'll see people bump numbers up for the full year. This is a very solid performance."
Analysts particularly were pleased with PepsiCo's beverage results in the international arena, where the company hopes to challenge rival Coca-Cola Co.
"It was much less of a loss than was originally expected," Goldman said of the international results.
PepsiCo is restructuring, shedding its restaurants to focus on beverages and snack foods.

Internationally, the new approach "is bearing fruit earlier than expected," Goldman said. "And that's very important for them, because it's been a source of major aggravation for them, to say the least."
Also pleasing to Wall Street was the performance of PepsiCo's restaurant units KFC, Taco Bell and Pizza Hut, which it plans to spin off into a separate company.
"You could really see the turn at Taco Bell," Goldman said. "The timing couldn't be better, because the spin-off is scheduled for the fourth quarter."
PepsiCo announced the spin-off in January, saying it would create the world's largest restaurant business.

PepsiCo Chairman Roger Enrico said at the time that PepsiCo needed to return to its roots, focusing on soft drinks and snacks, which constituted a fundamentally different kind of business than restaurants.
Enrico said the newly restructured PepsiCo would be aggressive on the international front, taking on Coca-Cola in such markets as China, India and Eastern Europe.

PepsiCo's first quarter international beverage results showed an operating loss of $27 million on net sales of $367 million, compared to a loss of $10 million on sales of $426 million for the same period the year before.
In North America, PepsiCo had beverage operating profits of $264 million on sales of $1.59 billion, compared to profits of $257 million on sales of $1.54 billion the year before.
Restaurants internationally had operating profits of $44 million on sales of $517 million, compared to profits of $36 million on sales of $501 million the year before.
Snack foods internationally had profits of $99 million on sales of $709 million, compared to profits of $73 million on sales of $628 million for first-quarter 1996.
